title: Resetting a total inside the loop
summary: Why a total that is reset inside a loop keeps only the last value, and how to place its starting value correctly.
objectives: Explain why resetting an accumulator inside a loop loses earlier values.
Trace how a total changes on each loop pass.
Place an accumulator's initialization before the loop.
Recognize the same reset mistake in maximum and minimum calculations.

blocks.text: Here is the exact pattern Code Coach flags:

The loop resets `total` to zero on every pass. Then it adds just the current sale. After the loop, `total` is `8`, not the intended sum `16`. This code compiles. Java does not warn that the result may be wrong; the mistake shows when the program runs.

blocks.title: The comment is not a Java exception
blocks.text: The comment says the running total is thrown away. That describes the logic, not a crash. The loop runs normally and leaves the last sale in `total`.

A `for` loop has an initialization part in its header. In `for (int i = 0; i < sales.length; i++)`, `i` is set to zero once, before the first condition check. The loop body runs again for each sale. Any assignment inside that body runs again too.

blocks.caption: The reset happens again on every pass
blocks.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  A[Set i to zero once] --> B{i less than sales length}
  B -- yes --> C[Reset total to zero]
  C --> D[Add current sale]
  D --> E[Increase i]
  E --> B
  B -- no --> F[Loop ends with total eight]

blocks.caption: int[] sales = {5, 3, 8};
blocks.name: sales
blocks.note: The loop visits `sales[0]`, `sales[1]`, and `sales[2]`. The last visit adds `sales[2]`, which is `8`, after resetting `total`.

blocks.title: The fix
blocks.text: Give `total` its starting value before the loop. Then let each pass add to the value already stored. `total += sales[i]` means `total = total + sales[i]`.

sections.title: Trace it, one pass at a time

blocks.text: A trace table records the important values after each pass. Follow both assignments in the body: first the reset, then the addition.

blocks.caption: Tracing the flagged code with sales equal to 5, 3, 8

blocks.text: The reset makes each pass forget the previous result. Move `total = 0` before the loop, and the additions become `0 + 5`, then `5 + 3`, then `8 + 8`. The final value is `16`.
First, compare complete programs. Both compile and run. The only important change is where `total = 0` appears.

bad.title: Resets on every pass

good.title: Keeps the running total

blocks.note: In the fixed program, `total` starts at zero before the loop and is not reset inside it. Each `+=` adds the next sale to the amount already stored.

blocks.text: The same reasoning applies to a running maximum. Start from the first value, then compare the remaining values. Starting from the first value matters when every value is negative.

This maximum example assumes the array has at least one value. `highest` is initialized before the loop and updated only when a larger value is found. If you reset `highest` inside the loop, earlier comparisons would be forgotten.
The reset can hide among other loop work. Look for a starting assignment such as `sum = 0`, `count = 0`, or `maximum = ...` inside the loop body.

bad.title: A count that restarts each pass

good.title: A count that keeps growing

blocks.note: The bad version can only leave `count` as zero or one. The fixed version keeps the count from earlier passes.

bad.title: A maximum reset to zero each pass

good.title: A maximum that remembers earlier values

blocks.note: For a non-empty array, initializing from `values[0]` gives the maximum a real value to compare with. Resetting it in the body discards the previous maximum.

blocks.title: A quick check
blocks.text: Ask: should this value remember earlier loop passes? If yes, initialize it before the loop and update it inside the loop.

blocks.question: What does `total` print after this program runs?
blocks.explanation: The code compiles. Each pass resets `total`, so the last pass leaves the final sale, `8`, in `total`.

blocks.question: Where should the starting assignment for a running sum go?
options: Inside the loop body, before each addition
blocks.explanation: Initialize the sum before the loop. Then each pass can add to the value from earlier passes.

blocks.question: What is the final value of `sum`?
blocks.explanation: The first pass changes `sum` from `0` to `2`. The second adds `4` to the stored `2`, giving `6`.

items: The initialization part in a `for` header runs once before the first condition check.
An assignment inside the loop body runs on every pass.
Resetting `total` inside the loop makes the final result depend only on the last value added.
Initialize an accumulator before the loop, then update it inside the loop.
For a running maximum or minimum, usually initialize from the first array value rather than from `0`.
This mistake usually compiles without a warning. Trace the values to find the run-time logic error.
